topPRs.title: test(interop): follow-mode supernode interop on ELSync + #21119 proof
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
## Summary
Switches the follow-mode supernode interop devstack presets to EL sync and adds the end-to-end proof that a light op-node sequencer adopts the supernode's deposits-only invalid-message replacement.

Fixes #21119

## Changes
**Devstack**
- Production-faithful light-sequencer topology: each follow-mode sequencer runs its own EL, distinct from the supernode VN's EL, joined only by L1 and P2P (CL gossip + EL block-body sync) — plus the supernode-EL frontend wiring.
- Default the light-sequencer and follow-L2 presets to **EL sync** with `SyncModeReqResp=false`, matching the req-resp CL-sync deprecation direction. Virtual-sequencer presets stay on CL sync (the VN is itself the genesis sequencer there; generic ELSync-from-genesis bootstrap is out of scope). Adds a `SyncMode` override to `l2CLNodeStartConfig`.

**Tests**
- `TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement`: follow-mode analogue of the virtual reorg test, sharing `runInteropInvalidMessageReplacementScenario`.
- Cross-node convergence + forward-progress assertions in the shared scenario: each chain's block producer converges with the supernode verifier route at cross-safe while advancing local-unsafe, and agrees at local-safe.
- Post-reorg check is **settle-first**: the convergence assertions run *before* sending the new transaction, so the tx lands on an already-converged chain. The new-tx step then uses the same idiomatic DSL helpers as the replacement-block assertion (`Transfer` → `AwaitValidatedTimestamp` → `AssertTxInBlock`).

## De-flaked under load (progress-aware, not wider margins)
The post-reorg chain settles over a few bounded reorgs, and on a saturated CI executor that recovery can be several times slower. Rather than widening a wall-clock deadline, the convergence assertions use **`MatchedWithProgressFn`**, which is progress-aware: it fails on a genuine stall (no forward progress within the stall window), not on total elapsed time. This tolerates a slow/loaded box while still catching real non-convergence. Reordering to **settle first, then transact** removes the previous race where the new tx competed with in-flight reorgs — which was the source of the long-tail slow runs. Validated **8/8** on kona+op-reth, every run a tight ~56s with no slow-run tail (the prior approach had passing ~55s but slow ~160s runs). op-reth is structurally sound in every run (invalid msg reorged out, deposits-only replacement adopted, follow-reorgs bounded, no forkchoice stall).

## op-geth: skipped (consistently fails — known gap)
The light-sequencer test is **skipped on op-geth** (`sysgo.SkipOnOpGeth`). On op-geth this scenario **consistently does not converge (0/12 locally; op-reth passes)**:

- After the deposits-only replacement, the op-geth follower **never adopts the supernode's replacement block**. Cross-safe stalls at the replacement height (e.g. block 9) while the sequencer keeps building a divergent chain above it, so the follow-source reorg fires every tick and **nothing past the replacement is ever validated** (`safe block not in canonical chain` repeatedly).
- The new transaction therefore never gets a stable receipt.
- The invalid message is invalidated exactly once (no re-inclusion loop), so this is a **block-propagation / convergence** gap, not a re-mint loop.
- The **virtual-sequencer** variant (`TestSupernodeInteropInvalidMessageReplacement`) passes on op-geth, so the gap is specific to the **light-sequencer follow path**.

op-geth is being deprecated, so we skip rather than block CI on it; the convergence gap is left for follow-up. The fix and test fully cover op-reth, the target client for this configuration.

## Test plan
`DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-reth RUST_JIT_BUILD=1 go test ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/supernode/interop/reorg/ ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/supernode/interop/follow_l2/`
- Light-sequencer #21119 test: **PASS** on op-reth — 8/8 in a kona+op-reth stress loop, ~56s each, no slow-run tail · virtual control: PASS · follow_l2 (DerivesSafeChain, HeadsDivergeThenConverge, P2PSync): PASS.
- op-geth: light-sequencer test skipped; virtual + follow_l2 unaffected.

---
Part 3 of 3. Stacked on the divergence-reorg PR (`fix/op-node-follow-sequencer-divergence-reorg`). Requires both op-node fixes underneath for these presets to start and converge.

## Stack (merge bottom-up)
1. #21120 — op-node: genesis bootstrap for ELSync follow-mode sequencers
2. #21121 — op-node: divergence reorg-reset for follow-mode sequencers
3. #21122 — devstack: switch follow-mode supernode presets to ELSync + #21119 end-to-end proof

topPRs.title: [DRAFT] go.mod: bump op-geth to Karst kill-switch (op-geth#802)
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
## ⚠️ Draft — CI probe, do not merge

Repins op-geth to the **Karst deprecation kill-switch** commit from [ethereum-optimism/op-geth#802](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/802) (`b698d07e9264`).

op-geth is being deprecated as of the Karst fork. With that PR, the beacon consensus engine refuses to build, seal, or import any block whose timestamp activates Karst (via `verifyHeader`, `Prepare`, and `FinalizeAndAssemble`), keyed off the existing `IsOptimismKarst` predicate — so it engages automatically wherever `KarstTime` is configured.

### Purpose of this draft
Surface the full set of monorepo tests that configure Karst (e.g. test chain configs with `KarstTime` set, or "all forks active" timestamps) and therefore now hit the kill switch. Once CI gives the complete picture, we'll decide how to adapt the affected tests / harnesses.
